{{Quote|First time racing, rookie poodoo?|Fud Sang|translated=1|audio=FudSang-taunt.flac|<ref name="E1R" />}}
A [[Gender/Legends|male]] member of a diminutive [[Species/Legends|species]], '''Fud Sang''' was an [[Prisoner/Legends|inmate]] at a maximum-security [[Prison/Legends|detention center]] known as [[Desolation Alley]], located on the [[Oovo IV/Legends|fourth]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Oovo]]. While incarcerated around [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], during the final [[Time/Legends|decades]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Sang was considered a mediocre [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] at best. Nevertheless, the prison [[Warden/Legends|warden]], [[Fenn Booda]], occasionally granted Sang the opportunity to participate in [[Podracing/Legends|Podraces]] that Booda hosted in the prison, which provided the inmates a form of entertainment. Piloting a [[BRE Block6 Tri-Ram|BRE Block6 ''Tri-Ram'']] [[Podracer/Legends|Podracer]], Sang managed to garner intimate knowledge of [[Vengeance (Oovo IV)|one of the moon's courses]] and became quite successful there. Sang's success eventually led him to being allowed to race on the [[Water/Legends|ice]] world [[Ando Prime/Legends|Ando Prime]], where his improving piloting skills also acquired him popularity.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Fud Sang is down there. Well, I thought he was serving four life sentences here at Oovo IV.|Fode Annodue|audio=Fode-FudSang.flac|<ref name="E1R" />}}
[[File:Fud_Sang_the_Magnificent.png|thumb|left|170px|Anakin Skywalker once possessed a statue of Fud Sang.]]
Fud Sang was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] member of a [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of small stature. Despite his meek appearance, Sang landed four consecutive life sentences and was sent to the maximum-security [[Prison/Legends|prison]] [[Desolation Alley]] on the fourth [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Oovo]], known as [[Oovo IV/Legends|Oovo IV]],<ref name="Prima">[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> sometime before [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="NEC1">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] to the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. The racing season presented in the [[Star Wars video games|game]] ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|Star Wars Episode I: Racer]]'' must have taken place during this year due to the appearances of [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], which correspond to ''The Phantom Menace''.</ref> There, he was placed under the watchful [[Eye/Legends|eye]] of the prison [[Warden/Legends|warden]] [[Fenn Booda]]. The warden was known to occasionally entertain the inmates with [[Podracing/Legends|Podraces]], and at some point Sang proved his worth as a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], prompting Booda to offer the diminutive fast-talker a chance to race the courses with the off-world pilots that came to compete on the barren moon. Well through his prison sentence, Sang accepted the offer and was presented an old [[Bokaan Race Engineering]] [[BRE Block6 Tri-Ram|BRE Block6 ''Tri-Ram'']]. The Block6 was not in pristine condition, and Sang often found himself maintaining it with scrap and outdated parts. Nevertheless, with the customizations it proved to be a formidable craft due to its high-end traction, above-average turning, and acceptable cooling, which compensated for the [[Podracer/Legends|vehicle's]] slow acceleration and a low overall top speed. Ultimately, the vehicle's attributes often did not matter, as Sang was not considered much of a pilot.<ref name="Prima" />

[[File:HuntingWabbitsRacer.png|thumb|right|200px|Fud Sang inspects his ''Tri-Ram'' Podracer.]]
Desperate to counter the professional off-world pilots regardless of his lack of skill, Fud Sang did everything possible to push his machine to its limits.<ref name="Prima" /> Booda even hinted at the possibility of granting Sang his freedom if the prisoner performed well.<ref name="Nint">[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer Official Nintendo Player's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'' Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]</ref> Although he was not considered a threat on the course by some, Sang managed to acquire thorough knowledge of a track known simply as [[Vengeance (Oovo IV)|Vengeance]]; he more or less memorized the layout of the course as it swung in and around Desolation Alley, and his victories there earned him the status of track favorite. In fact, it was a thorough knowledge of the Oovo IV courses in general that gave him an edge during races, sometimes making up for his mediocre piloting skills. He even scored a record race [[Time/Legends|time]] of ''03:51.921'' minutes for the Vengeance course.<ref name="Prima" /> Sang was occasionally allowed to race off of Oovo IV, and he gained some fame on the frozen world of [[Ando Prime/Legends|Ando Prime]], where he became a favored racer on [[Ando Prime drag course 2|one of the planet's drag courses]]. Sang even challenged other racers to compete against him.<ref name="E1RGBC">[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'']] {{C|Gameboy Color version}}</ref> Fud Sang gained enough racing popularity that a small statue was made in his image. One such statue was collected by fellow Podracer pilot [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]].<ref name="PH1">{{Twitter|infinata|status/385478371443884033|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|nobackup=1}}</ref>

Whenever the [[Troig/Legends|Troig]] race announcer [[Fodesinbeed Annodue/Legends|Fode Annodue]] spotted Sang on Oovo IV, Fode generally commented on Sang's prison sentence.<ref name="E1R" /> By the year [[24 BBY/Legends|24 BBY]],<ref name="24-BBY-Date">''[[Star Wars: Racer Revenge]]'' mentions in the opening crawl that the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] from [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] took place eight [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the events of ''Revenge''. ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places ''The Phantom Menace'' in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. Therefore, ''Revenge'' took place during the year [[24 BBY/Legends|24 BBY]].</ref> Sang's black and purple flag could be found on a racecourse located on the planet of [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]]. The course was located in the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Orotoru G'am]], and the flag was located near the [[Hall of Heroes (Dac)|Hall of Heroes]].<ref name="RR">''[[Star Wars: Racer Revenge]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
[[File:FudSangWalletPhoto.png|thumb|right|alt=Sprite image of Fud Sang's head from Star Wars Episode I Racer.|Fud as he appeared in 32 BBY]]
Fud Sang, despite meek outer appearances, was saddled with four consecutive life sentences on Oovo IV. Energetic and known for his gratuitous conversing,<ref name="Nint" /> Sang was desperate to defeat any off-worlders that arrived on his turf. He constantly upgraded his Podracer with whatever parts he could find, whether they were of quality or not.<ref name="Prima" /> He sometimes taunted competitors before races.<ref name="E1R" />

Fud was short, with a round fat body. His [[Limb/Legends|arms]] were much longer than his legs; indeed, each arm was nearly the size of his entire body. Sang also had two white [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] on bulbous stalks, and a narrow snout. His skin was [[Color/Legends|purple]].<ref name="E1R" />

==Equipment==
[[File:FudSangTaunt.png|thumb|left|200px|Fud Sang]]
When given his chance to race on Oovo IV, Warden Booda presented Fud Sang with an old Bokaan Race Engineering BRE Block6 ''Tri-Ram'' Podracer. The [[Engine/Legends|engine's]] primary color was black, with the front ends of the engines painted light blue. The exhaust tubes on the back of the engines were also blue. The [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] had a similar color combination, with the rear end of the cockpit painted black and the front end painted the same blue as the engines. The vehicle was constantly in disrepair, and Sang often had to fix it with scrap and outdated parts. Still, despite low speed and weak acceleration, the vehicle had very good traction and overall handling, granting Sang a good amount of control over his racer.<ref name="Prima" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:FudSangart.png|thumb|right|150px|Concept art from ''The Phantom Menace'']]
Fud Sang was designed for the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']],<ref name="PHROTJ1">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1590583722071687168|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|archivedate=20230719173840}}</ref><ref name="PHROTJ2">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1518452599208353792|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|archivedate=20220425045220}}</ref> but went unused until the design was revisited for the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. Fud Sang's appearance in ''The Phantom Menace'' made it as far as conceptual art<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|odymandrell|Mandrell, Ody}}</ref> and a conceptual sculpt.<ref name="ReusedBlog">{{SW|url=news/back-from-the-drawing-board-recycled-star-wars-aliens|text=Back from the Drawing Board: Recycled ''Star Wars'' Aliens|int=Back from the Drawing Board|nolive=1}}</ref> Ultimately, a maquette of the character dating back to ''Return of the Jedi'' appeared during scenes in Anakin Skywalker's bedroom.<ref name="PH1" /><ref name="PH2">{{Twitter|infinata|status/385614563556589569|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|nobackup=1}}</ref><ref name="PHROTJ2" />

Fud Sang received a far more substantial appearance as a playable character in the 1999 [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|Star Wars Episode I: Racer]]'',<ref name="E1R" /> which was released on the [[May 19|same day as]] ''The Phantom Menace''.<ref name="Year by Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref><ref name="IGN">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/games/star-wars-episode-i-racer|text=Star Wars: Episode I: Racer – Nintendo 64 – IGN|work=[http://www.ign.com IGN]|archivedate=20200524203904}}</ref> Sang could be unlocked during the first circuit of races, his track introducing players to Oovo IV. Sang could only be unlocked if the player could place ahead of him. Fud Sang was voiced by [[Jim Ward (voice actor)|Jim Ward]] in ''Racer'', the same voice actor who portrayed [[Mars Guo/Legends|Mars Guo]].<ref name="E1R" />

According to a [[2006]] [[Star Wars: Blogs]] article titled "Alien species concepts that became part of the SW universe," written by [[Tim Veekhoven]] as a part of his Source Blog series, Sang may have had a species name and an actual [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] known as Sanhueli and Hueli IV, respectively.<ref name="Blog">{{Blog|teekay-421|69|Alien species concepts that became part of the SW universe}}</ref> The blog article is considered non-[[canon]], due in part that the draft information was scrapped.
